items.title: Telangana: Third baby dies in Adilabad’s RIMS hospital fire
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. In the tragic fire that claimed the lives of two babies at Telangana’s Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS), a third infant also died while being shifted to the hospital. A two-day-old girl who was born prematurely at 28 weeks and weighed 1.1 kg was in a critical condition and died while being shifted to a nearby hospital. Two babies were already killed in the fire that broke out at the Special Newborn Care Unit (SNCU) ward of RIMS, a government hospital located in Adilabad on Monday, September 21. Both were preterm babies on ventilator care. Adilabad district Collector Rajarshi Shah told the media there were at least 27 babies in the SNCU at the time of the tragedy. The surviving infants were moved to private hospitals, he had said. The fire broke out at around 11.40 pm on the night of September 21. According to reports, the fire was caused after an air-conditioner in the reception area of the SNCU burst into flames. The exact cause of the fire is yet to be determined. Additional Collector Rajeshwar said that some of the hospital staff broke the glass walls of the ward to bring the babies out. Chief Minis
